summary.headline: GFL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 1,588 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR 219 crore on R32-led fluorochemicals growth.
summary.overview: Chemical segment revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 1,574 crore with EBITDA up 29% to INR 458 crore and segment PAT up 33% to INR 261 crore. Fluorochemicals was the standout, with revenue up 52% YoY and 44% QoQ on R32 sales, and existing R32 capacity is already at peak utilisation. Battery materials remain pre-revenue to small (INR 20-30 crore per quarter cited by an analyst), with a ramp promised from Q4 FY27 and a significant step-up in FY28. The Oman battery project has been put on hold and its capex is being moved to India, and the approved sovereign funding for Oman will not transfer.

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by mix shift to higher-value grades and new-age applications (semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen, batteries). Management guides 15-20% (later 17-20%) annual growth.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (R32 and refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 44% QoQ, mainly R32. Existing R32 capacity is fully utilised; a R32 expansion (about 20,000 t total capacity cited by an analyst) is due in Q2 FY27. R134A is on track for commissioning in FY27.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY and 1% QoQ, primarily on better realisations; described as steady.

segments.name: Battery materials
segments.commentary: LiPF6 has nearly completed qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF qualification is close; LFP and cathode active material revenue expected toward end-FY27. Current revenue is small, with dispatches on CIF terms recognised in the next quarter.

guidance_outlook: R32 capacity expansion to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; management expects full utilisation of the incremental R32 capacity in calendar 2027.
R134A capacity to be commissioned in FY27 (management said it is targeting earlier than year-end); capacity size not yet disclosed.
Battery materials: management says it is on track for a 3-digit INR crore quarterly revenue in Q4 FY27, with significant ramp-up in FY28 and full potential from FY28 onwards.
Gross block of INR 836 crore expected to rise to about INR 1,200 crore by end-FY27 as CWIP is capitalised.
FY27 capex plan held at about INR 2,300 crore in EV/battery and about INR 800 crore in chemicals; total announced plan of INR 6,000 crore over the next two years.
AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid) capacity to come in phases, first set by end-FY27 or Q3, mainly for captive use.
capex_capacity: R32 capacity expansion due Q2 FY27; existing R32 capacity at peak utilisation.
R134A brownfield project at an existing refrigerant site, to be commissioned in FY27; TCE feedstock to be imported, not backward integrated.

Oman battery materials project (about USD 216 million capex) put on hold; capex being redirected to India. Sovereign funding of about INR 1,200 crore approved for Oman will not be available for India.
Land for battery expansion available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) site; a second Dahej site is being added for FY27-end/FY28.
Fluoropolymer debottlenecking is done continuously, roughly every second quarter; new-age fluoropolymer capex sized in the previous quarter at about INR 250 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer price increases were marginal and pass-through of input cost increases (methanol, sulfur, oil-linked inputs since March 2026); management said formula-based contracts protect margins.
R32 is sold globally: about 40-50% under long-term contracts, remainder spot or contract-to-contract. Domestic and export pricing described as 'very close'.
Management said 3M's exit is past and it has taken the impact; AGC's announced UK facility shutdown has begun generating customer enquiries, with traction expected in a quarter or two.
Domestic BESS demand projected at 220-250 GWh by 2030 (versus earlier global ~1,800 GWh view).

qa_highlights.question: Have Chinese peers' fluoropolymer price increases been passed on by GFL, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said only a marginal increase was taken to recover input costs; growth is mainly from higher-value grades where competition with Chinese players is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth visible for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said it is absolutely visible; new fluoropolymer capacity is nearly fully utilised and further capacity will be added for semiconductor and battery applications, without disclosing specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Oman funding shortfall require a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said fundraising is ongoing and project-by-project; he does not see funding as a constraint for India capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How is fluoropolymer growth split between volume, price and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it precisely, saying growth is primarily mix (higher grades) plus volume from new fluoropolymers, not price.

qa_highlights.question: Will R32 capacity be fully utilised in calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said full utilisation is expected as capacity is commissioned, based on contracts and market understanding.

risks_watch: Oman project shift to India: loss of about INR 1,200 crore sovereign funding for that project and need for new funding of about INR 4,000 crore for battery chemicals.

R32 and R134A quota allocation under the formula (baseline and production over 2024-26) is not yet clear; management declined to say which new players will receive quota. An analyst also raised a question on consumption quota that management could not answer and will follow up on.
Battery materials revenue remains small; ramp is contingent on customer qualification (about 1.5 years stabilisation cited) and CIF-term revenue timing.
Standalone-to-consolidated revenue gap widening sequentially, which management attributed to CIF consignments booked in Germany and US subsidiaries.
Raw material cost volatility (sulfur, fluorspar, methanol) with only formula-based or marginal pass-through in fluoropolymers.
